questions.question: When is vibe coding (no structure, just AI-generated code) appropriate?
choices: For production systems with multiple developers
For quick prototypes, throwaway scripts, and learning exercises
For any code that will be maintained long-term
questions.explanation: Vibe coding works for quick prototypes, throwaway scripts, learning exercises, and one-off utilities where long-term maintenance isn't needed.

questions.question: What makes vibe engineering different from vibe coding?
choices: It's slower but produces more code
It adds structure: interfaces, tests, decomposition before AI generation
It requires a specific programming language
questions.explanation: Vibe engineering adds deliberate structure — defining interfaces, writing tests, planning decomposition — before having AI generate code. This makes code maintainable and reliable.

questions.question: What is the biggest risk of vibe coding in production?
choices: Code lacks tests, error handling, and structure, making it hard to maintain
questions.explanation: Production code without tests, error handling, and proper structure becomes increasingly difficult and dangerous to maintain as the project grows.
